item.title: Palo Alto Networks confirms PAN OS management interfaces affected by PHP2Shell RCE vulnerabilities
item.description:
Enterprise firewall vendor advisories updated today confirm perimeter management interfaces are affected by recent core web engine vulnerabilities. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit malformed HTTP request headers to corrupt memory structures within management web daemons.
The security advisory impacts Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software managing Next-Generation Firewalls. The underlying vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, stem from uninitialized memory allocation defects in PHP request processing handlers. Unauthenticated remote actors transmit malformed POST requests to trigger use-after-free memory corruption, executing arbitrary system commands under administrative privileges before application logic processes incoming traffic. Vendor bulletins detail scheduled emergency hotfixes rolling out between October 26 and October 28.
Subverting firewall management portals undermines perimeter network controls and access boundaries. Because PAN-OS appliances terminate VPN connections and manage access control lists, an unauthenticated administrative compromise allows threat actors to disable security inspection engines, harvest local credentials, and move laterally across internal subnets.
- Restrict public internet access to PAN-OS management interfaces immediately, placing management ports on isolated out-of-band VLANs. - Apply official PAN-OS maintenance hotfixes 10.2.18-h13, 11.1.16-h4, and 11.2.10-h16 as vendor release builds become available. - Inspect web server access logs for malformed multipart HTTP POST requests targeting administrative management endpoints. - Invalidate active administrative session cookies and execute mandatory account password resets across managed firewalls.
Perimeter firewall defense requires immediate out-of-band management isolation and rapid hotfix deployment to ensure edge security controllers remain protected against unauthenticated remote code execution. #CodeDefence #PaloAltoNetworks #PANOS #PHP2Shell #RCE #Firewall #PerimeterSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Developer platforms revoke thousands of stolen AI model API keys after Railway and OpenRouter breaches
item.description:
Cloud platform incident disclosures published today confirm coordinated credential exfiltration targeting non-human identities. Threat actors breached developer infrastructure vaults to extract active third-party API integration tokens used for artificial intelligence services.
The security breaches impacted developer platforms Railway and OpenRouter. Unauthenticated remote adversaries exploited stolen platform credentials to access environment variable vaults, exfiltrating active API access keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini model environments. Threat telemetry indicates adversaries harvested the stolen keys to run high-tier model inference workloads on victim billing accounts and query historical prompt contexts. Platform engineering teams forced global token revocations and reset environment secret stores.
Subverting non-human identity stores exposes enterprise cloud billing controls and confidential data pipelines. When third-party platform databases are compromised, exposed integration keys allow threat actors to bypass tenant authentication, access confidential prompt context, and execute high-velocity resource billing calls.
- Rotate all artificial intelligence model API integration keys across production cloud environments and developer vaults immediately. - Enforce strict usage caps, rate-limiting rules, and IP whitelisting across model provider administration portals. - Inspect provider billing dashboards for anomalous token usage spikes or unverified API originations. - Store integration secrets exclusively within dedicated enterprise secret managers featuring automated rotation policies.
Non-human identity governance demands continuous secret rotation and zero-trust API credential management to ensure cloud platform breaches do not lead to downstream artificial intelligence infrastructure exposure. #CodeDefence #Railway #OpenRouter #AISecurity #IdentitySecurity #APISecurity #CloudSecurity #DevSecOps #AppSec

item.title: Storm 0940 state actors abused ConnectWise credentials to infiltrate over 2250 Microsoft 365 tenants
item.description:
Threat intelligence writeups published today expand the scope of an ongoing supply chain compromise targeting delegated cloud identity relationships. State-sponsored threat actors leveraged stolen vendor application credentials to bypass tenant multi-factor authentication controls globally.
Post-incident telemetry linked the supply chain intrusion campaign to threat actor cluster Storm-0940. Adversaries utilized compromised service credentials associated with ConnectWise Cloud Backup to authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID endpoints. Because client tenants granted standing delegated administrative permissions to the integration, adversaries executed administrative API calls across more than 2,250 enterprise Microsoft 365 cloud environments, exfiltrating mailboxes and SharePoint repositories without deploying malware binaries.
Relying on persistent delegated administrative permissions creates severe cloud identity exposure across managed service provider ecosystems. When a third-party vendor application credential is stolen, adversaries ride existing trust relationships directly into customer tenant environments without triggering password reset barriers.
- Revoke all delegated administrative privileges and active OAuth integration tokens associated with ConnectWise Cloud Backup immediately. - Enforce granular, time-bound Partner Admin relationships GDAP across all managed Microsoft Entra ID tenants. - Audit cloud sign-in logs for high-volume service principal API calls originating from unverified external IP addresses. - Restrict OAuth application consent policies to require explicit administrator approval for all multi-tenant application integrations.
Cloud identity governance requires continuous partner permission auditing and strict non-human identity monitoring to ensure enterprise cloud tenants remain protected against supply chain credential abuse. #CodeDefence #ConnectWise #Microsoft365 #Storm0940 #EntraID #SupplyChain #IdentitySecurity #CloudSecurity #AppSec
